commit_message:
Fix handling of max_fragment_length extension for PSK

A psk session was assumed to be a resumption which failed a check
when parsing the max_fragment_length extension hello from the client.

Relevant code from PR#18130 which was a suggested fix to the issue
was cherry-picked.

Fixes #18121

Reviewed-by: Matt Caswell <matt@openssl.org>
Reviewed-by: Viktor Dukhovni <viktor@openssl.org>
Reviewed-by: Tomas Mraz <tomas@openssl.org>
(Merged from https://github.com/openssl/openssl/pull/24513)

fix_commit_message:
Fix potential NULL pointer dereference in final_maxfragmentlen()

In the final_maxfragmentlen() function, s->session is checked
for NULL after it was dereferenced earlier.
So move this NULL check to the top of the function.

CLA: trivial

Fixes: fa49560451 (Fix handling of max_fragment_length extension for PSK)
Signed-off-by: Andrey Tsygunka <aitsygunka@yandex.ru>

Reviewed-by: Tomas Mraz <tomas@openssl.org>
Reviewed-by: Frederik Wedel-Heinen <fwh.openssl@gmail.com>
Reviewed-by: Paul Yang <kaishen.yy@antfin.com>
(Merged from https://github.com/openssl/openssl/pull/27272)
agent_reasoning: Merged diff composed mechanically by cherry-picking fix 28de1f5004c1 on top of intro fa495604516a via git's 3-way merge. Vulnerability (NullPointerDereference): In ssl/statem/extensions.c, the final_maxfragmentlen() extension-processing callback was changed (while fixing PSK handling of the max_fragment_length extension) to unconditionally dereference s->session at the top of the function in order to initialize s->session->ext.max_fragment_len_mode when it is unspecified. However, the function retained a later guard 'if (s->session && USE_MAX_FRAGMENT_LENGTH_EXT(s->session))', implying the author was aware s->session could be NULL in this code path, yet the new dereference above it was left unguarded. This results in a potential NULL pointer dereference / crash if final_maxfragmentlen() is invoked while s->session is NULL. Root cause: A new dereference of s->session was introduced above an existing NULL check for the same pointer, instead of placing the NULL check before any use of s->session. The refactor removed the old PSK-resumption-specific check (which happened to also reference s->session only after other guards) and replaced it with unconditional access, without re-validating that s->session could still be NULL at function entry in all call paths.
